summary: Order quote timeouts (onset 12:06:10Z) are caused by pricing-engine, not market-data-service. Config change cfg-3120 ramped feature flag flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 12:04:00Z (applied 12:04:16Z). Within ~1 minute pricing-engine began running the CPU-heavy GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path (20000 paths, 3-9s per call); CPU jumped from ~40% to ~99%, quote p99 rose from ~60ms to ~2600ms, exceeding the 2000ms internal quote budget and the 2500ms order-service timeout, yielding 12%+ 5xx and order-service quote timeouts. Request rate was flat (no load surge), market-data-service latency/errors were flat (ruling out the protobuf deploy dep-6111), and there were no restarts or memory pressure. The flag was never rolled back and the incident was still fully active at 13:59Z. Root cause category: config_change, origin in pricing-engine's Greeks v2 code path.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Feature-flag ramp of Greeks v2 (config_change) saturated pricing-engine CPU, causing quote deadline misses and order timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 (flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100) at 12:04:00Z enabled the CPU-heavy GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path (20000 paths, 3-9s each) for all traffic. Pricing-engine CPU jumped from ~40% to ~99%, quote p99 went from ~60ms to ~2600ms, exceeding the 2000ms internal budget and the 2500ms order-service timeout, producing quote timeouts and elevated 5xx. The fault originates in pricing-engine (the newly-fully-enabled Greeks v2 code path) but is triggered by the flag rollout.

quote p99 rises 60ms->2600ms, exceeding 2000ms internal budget
order-service 2500ms pricing-engine quote calls time out

assumptions: The greeks_v2 flag gates the GreeksV2Calculator path (strongly implied by identical naming and timing, not directly stated in a single log line)
No other change between 11:56 and 12:05 affected pricing-engine

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy (dep-6111) broke pricing-engine quote parsing
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-6111 switched market-data-service quote serialization to protobuf at 11:56:00Z, allegedly causing pricing-engine quote timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service latency and error_rate stayed flat/normal throughout; the onset (~12:05) follows the pricing-engine flag change (12:04), not the 11:56 deploy; the failing code path is a local GreeksV2 CPU computation, not serialization; and the timing gap (9 min) doesn't match. This is the report's human guess, unsupported by telemetry.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation due to increased request load
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Traffic growth pushed pricing-engine past provisioned capacity, causing CPU saturation and timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate was flat (~630-660 req/s) across the onset; no load surge. CPU rose because a far heavier computation (GreeksV2) was enabled by the flag, not because of more traffic.

assumptions: The greeks_v2 rollout flag gates the GreeksV2Calculator execution path (inferred from identical naming and 1-minute onset alignment; no single log line states this explicitly)
No pricing-engine deployment or other config change occurred between 11:56 and 12:05 that could independently raise CPU (deployments list shows none)
Downstream effects (order timeouts) are caused by pricing-engine latency, consistent with the dependency graph order-service->pricing-engine->market-data-service

Slow GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo warnings begin (3-9s per call)

Incident still active; cfg-3120 never rolled back

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back cfg-3120 (set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 or 0) and confirm pricing-engine CPU and quote p99 recover
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the direct trigger; reverting the flag should immediately stop the CPU-heavy GreeksV2 path and restore latency. Flag was never rolled back and incident is ongoing.

recommended_actions.action: Add a target of reducing GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path count / optimizing the calculator before re-enabling at scale
recommended_actions.rationale: 20000-path Monte-Carlo runs taking 3-9s and pinning CPU at 99% is not viable at full traffic; needs optimization or a sampled/async design.

recommended_actions.action: Require load/capacity validation and staged ramp with automated rollback for feature-flag ramps on latency-critical services
recommended_actions.rationale: A 5->100 jump in one step bypassed gradual exposure; canarying would have caught the CPU blowup before full ramp.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on pricing-engine CPU saturation and GreeksV2 calculator duration budget breaches
recommended_actions.rationale: CPU pinned at 99% and 3-9s calculator runs were only visible as slow logs; proactive alerting would shorten detection.

data_gaps: The initial all-services config-change query (tc-004) was partial (config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond); however the retried full query (tc-019) returned the complete set of 2 changes, so config completeness is confirmed.
No log/metric directly proves the greeks_v2 flag is the on/off switch for the GreeksV2Calculator code path; this linkage is inferred from naming and timing.

Root cause of why GreeksV2 is CPU-heavy (code regression vs. inherently expensive algorithm) cannot be determined from telemetry alone; no pricing-engine deployment in window means the code predates the window.
